name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam (former Tropenmuseum)
funding: Run by Stichting Nationaal Museum van Wereldculturen, named Wereldmuseum since 2023 and under the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science since the 2014 merger. VriendenLoterij is a supporting partner.
watch: In the Colonial Institute building, opened by Queen Wilhelmina in 1926 and shared with the Royal Tropical Institute (KIT) until 2014; 317,572 visitors in 2022.

propaganda.summary: The Colonial Institute's statutes charged its museum, opened 1926 with Ministry of Colonies funding, with promoting all interests stemming from the colonial possessions, an aim described as colonial propaganda; renamed in 1950.

name: Museum of the Macedonian Struggle
funding: A National Institution established on 31 July 2008. The Skopje 2014 accounts record 2,110,940 euros of public money spent on its building. The Ministry of Culture heads its partner list.
watch: The government counted over 200,000 visitors in its first five years; visits are by compulsory guided tour past 109 wax figures and 85 history paintings.

propaganda.summary: The VMRO-DPMNE government built the museum under its Skopje 2014 programme and opened it on 8 September 2011. Its compulsory guided tour ends with a party co-founder, merging nation, revolutionary movement and governing party.

name: World Heritage Rock Art Centre – Alta Museum (Verdensarvsenter for bergkunst – Alta Museum)
funding: An intercommunal company owned 50/50 by Alta Municipality and Finnmark County. FY2023 income NOK 34.3M against costs of NOK 33.9M (Regnskapsregisteret), with no split between grants and earned income.
watch: Runs the UNESCO rock art site at Hjemmeluft with delegated heritage powers; European Museum of the Year in 1993.
records_note: States its ownership and mission; accounts are filed in Norway's register. No sponsor list found.

name: Bodø2024 European Capital of Culture
funding: Budget NOK 310M: Bodø and Nordland NOK 50M each, the state NOK 100M, sponsors, the EU and own income about NOK 110M. SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge's Samfunnsløftet co-funded one project.
watch: It found 17 private sponsors and partners; its director said it was underfinanced and cut programme to avoid a deficit.
records_note: Nord University's evaluation puts the total cultural budget at NOK 331M; no full sponsor list was found.

name: Festspillene i Nord-Norge (Arctic Arts Festival)
funding: A foundation backed by the Ministry of Culture, three northern counties, Harstad Municipality and SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge, with Aker BP, UiT and local firms as partners. FY2023 income NOK 28.2M.
watch: An annual festival in Harstad since 1964; Aker BP's logo sits among its business partners, with no amount given.
records_note: Shows partner logos without amounts; accounts are filed in Norway's register.

name: KaviarFactory
funding: Privately owned and paid for by the Oslo collectors Venke and Rolf Hoff, who bought the closed cannery and opened it in 2013. Rolf Hoff's business makes signage and produces artworks.
watch: Rolf Hoff once chaired the Lofoten International Art Festival's board; the couple say a private kunsthall buys without a committee.
records_note: No accounts, board or funding page found. On 17 Nov 2026 kaviarfactory.com served casino spam beside the venue's name.

name: Lofoten International Art Festival (LIAF)
funding: Run by the North Norwegian Art Centre (NNKS), core funded by the Ministry of Culture and Equality and the Nordland, Troms and Finnmark counties. NNKS reported FY2023 income of NOK 13.9M.
watch: Scandinavia's longest-running biennial; the collector Rolf Hoff of KaviarFactory once chaired its board.
records_note: Names its organiser and the organiser's core funders; edition supporters are shown only as logos.

name: Perspektivet Museum
funding: A foundation set up in 1996 that owns Storgata 95; Tromsø Municipality appoints every board member not elected by staff. FY2023 income NOK 10.0M against costs of NOK 10.6M (Regnskapsregisteret).
watch: A city history and documentary photography museum in the national museum network, holding about 500,000 photographs of Tromsø.
records_note: Publishes its board, collection plan and outreach plan; accounts are filed in Norway's register.

name: Pikene på Broen (Barents Spektakel, Terminal B Kunsthall)
funding: Core grants from the Culture Ministry and the northern counties; in 2019 Finnmark County, the Foreign Ministry and the Barents Secretariat backed its festival and residency, SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge and Fritt Ord projects. FY2023 income NOK 14.4M.
watch: A curators' company 15 km from the Russian border; a long-standing main festival sponsor, unnamed, pulled out in 2019.
records_note: Publishes annual reports from 2010 to 2019 with board and funders; accounts are filed in Norway's register.

name: Riddu Riđđu
funding: A Sámi music and culture festival backed by Arts Council Norway, the Ministry of Culture, Troms County and Kåfjord Municipality, with Coop Nord as a partner. FY2023 income NOK 13.6M.
watch: Held every July in Kåfjord since 1991.
records_note: Shows funder and partner logos without amounts; accounts are filed in Norway's register.
